A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TMD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated algorithms and renumbered figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original VBench evaluations, a user preference study, and ablations of TMD and DMD2-v, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, user-study, and ablation results and adds inference-time measurements and pretraining-budget experiments in Tables 12–13.

M1.justification: The decoupled backbone, conditional flow head, TM-MF pretraining, DMD2-v objectives, and flow-head rollout remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move to Appendix A without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the teacher-generated video dataset with VidProM/Qwen prompts, 480p text-to-video generation, and VBench evaluation of Wan2.1 1.3B and 14B models. The added timing and pretraining-budget analyses introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the matched benchmark and ablation comparisons. New Table 13 reuses the existing two-step rCM and DMD2-v baselines and scores; Table 12 uses the existing teacher architecture as its timing reference.

E3.justification: Table 12 introduces component timing with M=1 and batch size 1 on a single H100. Table 13 evaluates 0.5k, 1k, and 3k TM-MF pretraining budgets with distillation reported as under 6k iterations. These supplement the retained evaluation protocols; the original Table 7 defaults are unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections B.7–B.8 add analyses of component latency and sensitivity to pretraining duration. Conversely, v1 Figure 13's gated-versus-concatenated fusion convergence plot is removed, although Table 9's final-score comparison and the stability discussion remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same five generation seeds per prompt for the 60-prompt user study. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates; its new tables report point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes the Wan2.1 14B TMD-N4H5 result at NFE 2.75 from 84.62/85.09/82.72 to 84.92/85.54/82.42 for overall/quality/semantic scores under the same reported configuration. Tables 12–13 add timings and reduced-pretraining results, including overall scores 84.52 and 84.59 at 0.5k and 1k pretraining iterations. The fusion convergence traces in v1 Figure 13 are removed.

T1.justification: The transition-matching definitions, MeanFlow derivation, distillation equations, effective-NFE formula, finite-difference approximation, and appendix curvature definition are retained. No substantive mathematical correction, assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same architectural and two-stage training contributions and speed–quality claims. The highlighted near-one-step 14B VBench result remains 84.24 at NFE 1.38.

C2.justification: Section B.7 newly interprets measured latency ratios as validating effective NFE as an efficiency proxy. Section B.8 adds the argument that TMD is training-efficient relative to rCM and remains competitive with substantially reduced pretraining. Existing mechanism explanations and qualifications are largely retained.

D1.justification: The new analyses disclose timing hardware, batch size, component runtimes, and additional training-budget information. Existing implementation details and Table 7 remain. The project-page link supplied with v1's abstract is absent from v2, removing an access pointer without establishing any change in the underlying resource's availability.

R1.justification: The same 70 cited works and the related-work discussion are retained. Section B.8 adds limited training-efficiency positioning against rCM, contrasting TMD's 3k pretraining plus 1k distillation iterations for 14B with rCM's cited 10k iterations.

P1.justification: v2 lightly edits the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, moves Algorithms 1–2 from the main text to Appendix A, and adds two appendix subsections. The principal section order and explanatory narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the NVIDIA report styling with a conference-style layout, changes typography and abstract columns, removes running headers and footers, and resizes or relocates figures and tables throughout. Figure 2 changes from full-width to single-column presentation. Tables 12–13 are added and v1 Figure 13 is removed; retained qualitative images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Tables 12–13 modestly strengthen the efficiency evidence by supplying actual H100 timings and testing reduced pretraining budgets. These gains are partly offset by removing the fusion-stability plot and project link. Section 4.2 also remains unreconciled with revised Table 2: it says TMD does not outperform two-step baselines although its updated overall score exceeds DMD2-v's. The added practical evidence provides a limited net improvement, while the method and most validation remain unchanged.
